newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Elektrowatt shares under pressure on report. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Elektrowatt shares under pressure on report. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]

text.p: Shares of Elektrowatt AG declined as they went ex-dividend and on a Swiss newspaper report that Siemens AG may try to lower its proposed purchase price for the company's industrial business, dealers said.
(Corrects to make clear shares going ex-dividend also played a role in decline)
Elektrowatt shares were down nine Swiss francs at 530 around midday, off a low at 528.
A spokesman for Credit Suisse Group, which is making the sale of Elektrowatt possible by disposing of its large holding in the group, declined comment on the report.
Credit Suisse Group has a 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt and has said it will offer to buy other outstanding shares at 550 francs each, subject to due dilligence.
This corresponds to a 285 franc per share price Siemens is to pay for the industrial business and 265 francs per share to be paid for its energy operations by a Swiss/German consortium.

The SonntagsZeitung report said Siemens wanted to reduce the price because property at Elektrowatt's Goehner-Merkur unit was overvalued and would have to be marked down if Siemens were forced to sell under Swiss laws on foreign property ownership.
An Elektrowatt spokesman said the potential buyers were aware of the ownership restrictions at the time negotiations took place and these were reflected in the takeover price.
A spokesman for Siemens in Munich declined comment, citing company policy not to comment on rumours and speculation.
